correctness.rationale: The proof correctly separates unbounded curves by the fundamental-ray geometry of the leading phase \(Q\). Away from a fundamental ray, one exponential dominates because \(R=o(Q)\). Along a fundamental ray of \(Q\), the no-common-ray hypothesis makes \(\Re R\) have a fixed nonzero sign of order \(r^{\deg R}\). If \(\Re R\to+\infty\), boundedness of \(e^Q+e^{-Q+R}+P\) would force the two exponentials to have asymptotically equal modulus and opposite phase, contradicting the phase separation supplied by the source's fundamental-ray lemma. If \(\Re R\to-\infty\), their product tends to zero while the polynomial term grows; one exponential must dominate on an unbounded connected tail, reducing boundedness to the one-exponential case covered by Theorem 1.1. This establishes the unbounded-image curve criterion and hence the Baker omitted value. The hypotheses exclude the cancellation examples where same-degree opposite phases differ only by a constant.
risks: The proof is a generic sufficient condition; it does not classify the same-degree opposite-leading-coefficient case when fundamental rays of \(Q\) and \(R\) coincide.
